Under the old 2011-12 series, GDP was estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore. However, under the new series, it has subsequently been revised to Rs 80 lakh crore.

title: ‘India lost to Ireland. Has cricket ended?’: Naqvi defends Pakistan's shake-up
content: Mohsin Naqvi, chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board, stood firm regarding the team's latest performances and selection adjustments. He questioned whether a handful of defeats should spell the end of cricket in Pakistan. Noting other teams' challenges, he highlighted Pakistan's advancements in white-ball rankings while also tackling critiques from former players about the management's approach to team building.

title: Why personal-guarantor recoveries are so tiny — and why Chandra’s was tinier still
content: Subhash Chandra was offering just 0.03% of the loans for which he was a personal guarantor. But there should be no surprise here. In the history of such settlements in India, guarantors have paid an average 1% of the amount they stood guarantee for

title: Tim Cook reveals the emails he reads every morning, a habit he’s kept for 15 years
content: Tim Cook is stepping down as Apple CEO after fifteen years. He will transition to the role of executive chairman.  Longtime insider John Ternus will assume leadership of the tech giant. Cook revealed his daily ritual of reading customer emails. This practice grounded him and connected him to Apple's users.

title: Wai Wai under FSSAI scanner: Firm told to stop production, 32,000kg stock seized
content: Food regulator FSSAI has ordered CG Foods India to stop producing Veg Bhujia Namkeen.  Inspections revealed hygiene lapses and unlicensed manufacturing of bhujia products.  The company was found re-processing floor-collected noodles without proper heat treatment.  FSSAI seized over 32,000 kg of stock and detained expired finished goods.  Legal proceedings have been initiated against CG Foods India for these violations.

title: 'Govt aid would stop': Bengal CM warns schools over Vande Mataram compliance
content: West Bengal's Chief Minister warned schools about financial aid cuts for not singing Vande Mataram. He criticized past governments for allegedly destroying the education system and distorting curricula. The Chief Minister stated reforms are underway to restore Indian culture and nationalist values in schools. He also accused the previous government of banning the National Cadet Corps in educational institutions.

title: ‘Akash Anand needs to become more mature’: Mayawati rules out major BSP role for nephew
content: In her recent remarks, Mayawati emphasized that Akash Anand needs greater political maturity to assume significant roles within the party. She reaffirmed that the Bahujan Samaj Party intends to independently contest all upcoming elections nationwide. Additionally, she labeled the Congress party as distinctly anti-Dalit and anti-Ambedkar, and critiqued the RSS for inconsistencies between their rhetoric and actions.

title: Bezos got a special invite to ‘US exclusive Country Club’ but won’t get membership
content: Jeff Bezos and Lauren Sanchez attended an exclusive club event as guests.  Six months later, Bezos still awaits membership despite owning island properties.  Membership at Indian Creek Country Club requires more than significant financial investment.  Other prominent residents also face challenges in securing club membership.  The club's stringent approval process emphasizes member relationships and committee decisions.

title: 'How am I responsible for my daughter's comments?' Sacked T'gana minister takes on CM
content: Former minister Konda Surekha expressed her displeasure regarding her cabinet removal. She stated she committed no corruption and had responded to show-cause notices. Surekha questioned the lack of consultation and the fairness of the decision. She defended her daughter and questioned actions against other Congress leaders. The former minister has not yet decided on her future political path.

title: Scientists treated New Hampshire watershed for acid rain; nitrogen later surged
content: In an ambitious forest restoration initiative in New Hampshire, researchers sought to mitigate the effects of acid rain. They introduced calcium-rich minerals, leading to an initial boost in tree vitality and growth. However, this solution inadvertently resulted in a staggering increase in nitrogen levels in nearby streams, releasing thirty times more inorganic nitrogen compared to untreated regions. This outcome underscores the intricate dynamics of ecosystems in response to human intervention.

title: SkyMall founder's Arizona ranch has 1,250-year-old tree and $9.475m price tag
content: Bob Worsley, the visionary behind SkyMall, is parting ways with his picturesque family ranch in Heber, Arizona. Spanning 35 acres, this stunning off-grid estate features a spacious lodge, several cabins, and boasts complete self-sufficiency with solar energy and its own well. The property offers a refreshing retreat from the desert's swelter and includes a natural gathering lake. It's currently on the market for $9.475 million.

title: Apple and Google rename Lake Ontario to Lake America; one app refuses Trump’s order
content: MapQuest's refusal to comply with a federal directive to rename Lake Ontario has landed the app at the peak of the US App Store charts. Unlike Google Maps and Apple Maps, which followed the presidential order, MapQuest experienced a remarkable boost, collecting over 1.5 million downloads in North America. The company is now shifting focus towards new features that users are eager for.

title: Building near airport? Centre plans faster height clearances, local-level NOCs
content: New reforms are set to expedite building height approvals in proximity to airports, streamlining the planning process for developers. They will now receive height permissions much earlier, especially in key metropolitan areas such as Delhi and Mumbai. Local urban bodies are expected to start issuing height no-objection certificates (NOCs), while automated digital tools will dramatically shorten project clearance timelines.

title: ‘Only a frikkin game’: Akram recalls helping India bowler before his anti-Pak posts
content: Legendary cricketer Wasim Akram urges fans to leave past conflicts behind when it comes to cricket. He emphasises that the India-Pakistan rivalry should be viewed simply as a sport. Reflecting on his mentorship of Irfan Pathan, who admired his bowling style, Akram noted Pathan's impressive hat-trick against Pakistan. Ultimately, he reminded everyone that victories and defeats are part of the game, encouraging fans to let go of grudges.

title: NBA hammers Clippers: Ballmer banned, picks stripped, Kawhi fined $700k
content: The NBA has delivered a harsh blow to the Los Angeles Clippers, penalizing them for salary-cap violations linked to Kawhi Leonard. The repercussions include forfeiting five first-round draft picks and substantial financial penalties, alongside suspensions for owner Steve Ballmer and several executives. Leonard himself faced a fine of $700,000. In response, the Clippers dispute the allegations and are gearing up to challenge the league's decision.

title: Tara Davis-Woodhall 'lucky to be alive' after head-on car crash
content: Olympic champion Tara Davis-Woodhall survived a serious car crash last week. She sustained a severe concussion in the head-on collision which damaged both vehicles. The accident occurred while she was driving to training at approximately twenty miles per hour. Davis-Woodhall is now focusing on recovery and assessing her ability to compete. Her participation in the World Athletics Ultimate Championship remains uncertain.

title: Ajay Devgn, Tiger Shroff respond to FDA's notice for elaichi ad, SRK's reply awaited
content: Ajay Devgn and Tiger Shroff have both responded to the notice issued by the Maharashtra FDA, while the wait continues for Shah Rukh Khan's reply. The notice raised concerns about the elaichi advertisement, suggesting it may be promoting Vimal Pan Masala, a product that is banned in Maharashtra. Further developments from the FDA are expected after Khan provides his response.

title: ‘Diversity is true beauty of society’: B'desh PM extends Janmashtami greetings
content: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman extended Janmashtami greetings to the Hindu community. He stated that the country belongs to all citizens, who enjoy equal rights. Rahman urged strengthening religious harmony, tolerance, and mutual respect among people. He warned against forces attempting to create divisions and communal tensions. The Prime Minister distributed honorariums to priests and sebaits.

title: India's answer to China's Type 15: Inside Belgian-powered Zorawar light tank
content: India is enhancing its defense relationship with Belgium, focusing on increased security collaboration. The two countries have finalized agreement terms to advance military exchanges and training programs, showcasing commitment. Notably, the indigenous Zorawar light tank, capable of high-altitude warfare, incorporates a turret designed by Belgian firm John Cockerill. Produced in India through a joint venture, India has already ordered 59 Zorawar tanks to address regional security challenges.

title: BRICS Summit 2026: Delhi, Central govt offices to remain closed on September 11
content: Central and Delhi government offices will close on September eleventh. This closure is due to the upcoming 18th BRICS Leaders Summit in New Delhi. Extensive security and logistical arrangements are being made for the international event. Leaders from approximately thirty countries will attend the summit and business forum. India is hosting the summit under its 2026 BRICS chairship.

title: VVS Laxman to step in as India head coach for Asian Games in Gambhir’s absence
content: VVS Laxman will coach the Indian men's cricket team at the 2026 Asian Games. Gautam Gambhir will remain with the senior team for the West Indies ODI series. The Indian men's team will defend its T20 title under Shreyas Iyer. Harmanpreet Kaur will lead the defending champion Indian women's team. Both teams are set to compete in the upcoming Asian Games.

title: US-Venezuela's historic deal: Will Americans get cheaper gas now?
content: The United States has successfully negotiated a deal to import Venezuelan oil, aiming to replenish its reserves with a consistent supply of affordable crude. While the long-term implications for American drivers remain ambiguous, the deal's effect may not be felt for several months. The arrangement involves significant untapped oil fields and a private company, but future political developments in both nations could pose risks to this energy collaboration.

title: Meet Shreyansh Gupta, IIT Madras student ranked in top 0.6% of Google hackathon
content: IIT Madras BS learner Shreyansh Gupta ranked 278th among 46,719 participants at the Google for Developers × Hack2skill PromptWars 2026 hackathon, placing him in the top 0.6%. His solution for improving large-scale sporting event experiences scored 88.81/100 in AI evaluation, including 100/100 for efficiency. Beyond hackathons, Shreyansh is building experience across AI agents, full-stack development, augmented reality and student technology initiatives, reflecting his focus on turning technical skills into practical solutions.

title: 'Like a thanedar': As Satyendar Jain gets bail, Arvind Kejriwal targets PM Modi

Bharadwaj also condemned the arrest, calling it unnecessary harassment. The case involves a tender awarded to Euroteck Environmental Private Limited. The Anti-Corruption Bureau alleged manipulation of tender conditions.

title: Dropped from squad, Pakistan player refuses to meet King Charles III
content: Pakistan’s cricket team faced fresh controversy when several players dropped from the Test squad were told to attend a meeting with King Charles III. Four attended despite preferring to stay away, while one refused in protest. The meeting came after Pakistan’s defeats to England triggered major squad changes, the sacking of coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and the appointment of Mike Hesson.

title: Toronto home sales fall for first time in six months as trade worries weigh
content: Greater Toronto Area home sales decreased in August for the first time in six months.  Concerns over trade and potential borrowing cost increases deterred many buyers.  Sales and prices also saw a year-on-year decline in the region.  New property listings experienced a significant drop during the same period.  This housing market slowdown reflects broader economic uncertainties.

title: Mumbai killer crash on camera: Car rams bike, autos at traffic signal; woman dead
content: A car crashed into vehicles at a Mumbai traffic signal on Sunday evening.  The collision tragically killed a 34-year-old woman and injured six others.  The driver reportedly claimed he mistook the accelerator for the brake pedal.  He was arrested and later released on bail after a medical examination.  The incident has prompted demands for stricter action against the driver.

title: 140kg deadlift: Who is Keyaa who lifted over 3 times her body weight for World silver?
content: Keyaa Kunal Banerji made headlines by lifting 140kg and snagging a silver medal at the world championships, an impressive feat that made waves on social media as it was over three times her own bodyweight. Meanwhile, Madhura Kar shone brightly, collecting four gold medals, and Asma Taherali Zabuawala secured a commendable sixth place in her weight category. Together, they exemplify India's rising prowess in global powerlifting arena.

title: Magnitude 5 quake hits Tibet amid ongoing search for hundreds missing after deadly floods
content: An earthquake of magnitude five struck Tibet on Thursday.  Rescue operations continue following catastrophic flooding near the Gyirong border crossing.  The only road to the crossing reopened, allowing heavy machinery access.  Authorities reported twenty-one deaths and 541 people remain missing.  Landslides continue to pose a significant concern for rescue teams.

title: Pune activist opposing loud DJs during Ganpati processions slapped, video surfaces

A video shows a man slapping Bapat during his statement to reporters. Police are working to identify the attacker and ensure Bapat's safety. Bapat's campaign against loud DJs has gained significant public support statewide.

title: Sugar gets sweeter again: Retail prices fall 3.85% to Rs 62.57/kg in a week
content: Sugar prices have started to fall across markets following government interventions.  The average retail price has dropped significantly over the past week.  However, consumers still pay more than a month ago due to existing stock.  Wholesale rates are not immediately reflecting in retail prices as traders hold old inventory.  Government measures like import allowances and stock curbs aim to stabilize prices.

title: Dealer failed to transfer car ownership; commission orders Rs 2.57 lakh payout
content: A car dealer must pay a customer Rs 2.57 lakh for failing to transfer ownership. The dealer also kept the customer's second-hand car at its workshop for years. This happened after the vehicle met with an accident shortly after delivery. The commission found the dealer's arguments regarding RTO inspection illogical. The dealer's appeal was dismissed, upholding the original order for payment and compensation.

title: India unveils 10-year ‘RAKSHA’ roadmap to expand global defence & security ties
content: Defence minister Rajnath Singh unveiled India's ten-year defence diplomacy roadmap. The RAKSHA document outlines strategic partnerships and capacity building initiatives. It promotes indigenous defence exports and strengthens maritime security cooperation. This framework aligns national security with proactive international engagement. India aims to be a key defence manufacturing hub and regional stability anchor.

title: Bridges & underpasses: Gadkari announces Rs 2,077cr project for Siliguri Corridor

The project includes bridges and elephant underpasses for safer wildlife movement. Congestion is expected to ease in Bagdogra and surrounding areas after completion. Faster movement of local produce to markets will be facilitated by this development.
